key_insight: The paper shows that vanilla on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) is just the β=1 case of a broader policy-optimization framework. By exposing β as a tunable KL-penalty weight, the method turns a brittle training recipe into a controllable one.
problem_solved: It addresses the instability and heavy engineering burden of making OPSD work reliably for reasoning language models.
method: Reformulate OPSD as policy optimization with a KL regularization term that anchors the student to a reference policy.
Generalize the objective with a β parameter, where β controls the strength of the KL penalty instead of fixing it implicitly at 1.
Use this equivalence to derive a more flexible training setup that can be tuned for stability and performance.
impact: For practitioners, this provides a cleaner way to understand and tune self-distillation training. It can reduce trial-and-error engineering and make reasoning-model improvement more reliable.
visual_elements: A side-by-side equation graphic showing vanilla OPSD vs. β-OPSD
A slider icon or scale illustrating β controlling the KL penalty
A workflow diagram: reference policy → student updates → self-distillation loop
A stability chart comparing brittle training vs. controlled optimization
paper_title: $β$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
paper_authors: Jiawei Xu, Minghui Liu, Juzheng Zhang, Tom Goldstein, Furong Huang
